doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

chapter: Cecil Taylor and the new music
title: Power of the new music and watching Cecil Taylor grow
summary: Spellman explains the power of late-50s/60s music and how he watched Taylor develop in Village coffeehouses.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well power I think, that was the thing about the new music, the late 50s and 1960s was that there was so much power in it. And your mind was never at rest when you were hearing it. Your mind was always open and moving, and always challenged. And I couldn’t get enough of it. I couldn’t find it in any other aspect of life.

Was there a set-up for you musically specifically with jazz artists? And when I say set-up I’ll share a brief little anecdote of myself that the first John Coltrane record I bought unknowingly was “Om.” And that was not a set-up.
Well you thought about going heaven, didn’t you.
Yes. And it scared me off a little bit, but I wonder, what set you up to enjoy Cecil Taylor?

Cecil Taylor? Well first of all, when I first got into Cecil Taylor he was not quite the powerhouse he was at the time that he was a few years later. He was still finding his voice and he was playing in little coffee houses around Greenwich Village and on some pretty raggedy pianos, and I got to watch him in the late 50s, I got to watch him grow, which is always a wonderful thing to do with another artist, to watch them grow, watch them actually empower themselves. And so by the early 60s you could see the power that I spoke of earlier was there. It was music that I had never heard before, it was music that didn’t exist anywhere else. He was not like anybody else, which is also a very rare thing to find, an artist who is not like another artist. Cecil wasn’t. So I just became thoroughly, thoroughly involved with what he was doing, and also I was getting to know him a little bit and that too is a great situation to have, to know an artist who is in the process of growing.
